_readme: Numbers for the player count screen and the three build minigames (PLAN.md section 7). Each minigame gives every player a score from 0 to 100; the team average becomes one mission number ("becomes"): build quality, structure strength or fuel loaded. Flight and launch use those numbers from TASKS.md step 7 on. All numbers here are game-design choices, not NASA numbers, and wait for the team's pass after playtesting. The words are in data/story.json ("player_count_screen" and "minigames").
source: PLACEHOLDER: game-design choice proposed at Step 11b (2026-11-13), not searched yet, waiting for the team's pass (the team tunes them after playtesting)
_button_delay_readme: How long the turn and score screens wait before their button works, so a player still pressing keys from the game doesn't skip the screen by accident. Game-design choice (2026-11-13).

players._readme: max = the most players on one computer (they take turns). card_width = how wide each card is on the How many players? screen, in pixels.

tutorial._readme: The tutorial card before each minigame (UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 17). example_height_pixels = how tall the tiny moving example is.

assembly._readme: Type the name of the part being bolted on (UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 18). Harder characters get longer words and less time. levels: easy = Scientist, medium = Janitor, hard = Student. words = the part names for that level (spaces are skipped while typing). duration_seconds = how long one turn lasts. target_parts = finished words for a full 100 score. wrong_key_freeze_seconds = how long a wrong key freezes you. part_shapes = which 3D shape snaps onto the workshop rocket for each word (fin, tank, rod, panel, dish, box); a word not listed gets a box.
assembly.source: PLACEHOLDER: game-design choice proposed at Step 11b (2026-11-13), words and times changed at UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 18 (2026-11-14), waiting for the team's pass

ship_tasks._readme: UPGRADE_PLAN_V6 C5: the small jobs at the ship's Life Support stations (scripts/ship_task.gd). fill_seconds = how long holding the valve takes to fill the gauge to the top; green_start / green_end = the green zone (0-1) to let go in; done_pause_seconds = the job stays on screen this long after it is done. Game-design choice.

hammer._readme: Hammer the nails on the rocket panel (UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 19). nails_per_turn = how many nails pop up in one turn (the 'Nails left' count). spawn_every_seconds = a new nail every this many seconds. nail_life_seconds = how long a nail stays before it slides back out (a miss). hit_radius_pixels = how close to a nail a click must be. nail_size_pixels = how big a nail head looks. dent_limit = the most dents shown at once (looks only; dents cost no points). Score = nails hit / nails_per_turn x 100.
hammer._panels_readme: UPGRADE_PLAN_V6 A7 (2026-11-15): the turn is a row of ship panels, not one panel with random nails. Every nails_per_panel nails the finished panel slides away and the next shape slides in; the nails sit in order along its seam. shapes = the outline of each panel, points from 0 to 1 inside the play area (they repeat if there are more panels than shapes). The small rocket in the corner fills one piece per finished panel. slide_seconds = how long a new panel takes to slide in.
hammer.source: PLACEHOLDER: game-design choice proposed at Step 11b (2026-11-13), changed at UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 19 (2026-11-14), waiting for the team's pass

fuel._readme: Drag the valve to the target angle, counterclockwise from the Start mark (0 degrees, on the right). rounds = how many targets per turn. round_seconds = time for one target (when it runs out, the valve's angle counts). min_angle and max_angle = the smallest and biggest target, in degrees. points_lost_per_degree = 100 points minus this for each degree you are off. result_seconds = how long the round's result shows. show_live_angle = true shows the angle while you drag (easier). dial_radius_pixels and handle_radius_pixels = the size of the valve on screen.
fuel.source: PLACEHOLDER: game-design choice proposed at Step 11b (2026-11-13), not searched yet, waiting for the team's pass

voice._readme: What the inner voice says on a minigame's results screen (lines in data/inner_voice.json, "minigames"). A team average of good_at or more gets the "good" line, below bad_below gets the "bad" line, anything between gets the "ok" line. good_at is also where a Fueling round beeps good instead of bad. Matches the flight's build_quality numbers in events.json (75 and 40).

workshop._readme: The 3D workshop behind every minigame (scripts/workshop_background.gd, TASKS.md step 12). Looks only: nothing here changes a score. Sizes and positions are in meters, [x, y, z]; the camera looks toward -z, and the back wall is at z = wall[1]. wall = [height, z]. Colors are web color codes. rocket: stages_shown = how many body stages stand up in each minigame (Assembly shows 1, and the top stage and nose wait on the floor at waiting_parts_offset [x, z] from the rocket). workers: scene = which toy-like person; path = the points they walk between (they work at each point for work_seconds); walk_speed in meters per second; work_face_degrees = which way they face while working (the person faces -z at 0; 180 = toward the camera, -90 = to the right, 90 = to the left); work_sound = a sound (data/game_data.json "sounds") played when this worker starts a job; radio_every_seconds = how often the workshop radio beeps (PLAN.md section 7: clanks, drills, radio chatter); carry = holds a crate; lift = stands on a platform that rides with them (give the path points different heights).
